extracted.intended_audience: U.S. tech entrepreneurs and startups seeking NSF SBIR/STTR seed funding
extracted.subtask_description: Information and evaluative guidance for startups applying to America's Seed Fund (NSF SBIR/STTR) for early-stage, non-dilutive seed R&D funding. Focuses on program scope, applicant eligibility, and the main dimensions reviewers consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment amount and equity terms
rubrics_metrics.description: We invest up to $2 million in seed funding. And take zero equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed capital for early stage product development; funding is non-dilutive so companies retain ownership. (Page emphasizes 'Start your grant process here' and highlights the up-to-$2M and no-equity terms as core program features.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible stage — early-stage R&D / seed
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer funding for early stage R&D — seed capital for early stage product development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is intended to support early R&D that moves technologies toward market readiness; success-story examples illustrate projects at early commercialization stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology focus — deep technologies grounded in fundamental science and engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: We support research and development of deep technologies - those that are based on discoveries in fundamental science and engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference/priority is on technologies founded on scientific and engineering discoveries rather than purely incremental or downstream product tweaks; examples on the page (materials science, biomaterials, VR education, medical devices, etc.) illustrate the kinds of 'deep tech' supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation dimensions: innovativeness, commercial potential, societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: As we review applications, we consider your technology’s innovativeness, commercial potential, and possible societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three dimensions are explicitly named as reviewer considerations. The page demonstrates them via success stories (e.g., devices that reduce harm, processes that replace banned chemicals, technologies enabling commercialization) to illustrate desirable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants — startups and entrepreneurs across the U.S., including first-time entrepreneurs
rubrics_metrics.description: We invite all tech entrepreneurs. Our program fosters and encourages participation in innovation and entrepreneurship from all Americans as well as first-time entrepreneurs from all 50 states and U.S. territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is open to early-stage companies and emphasizes inclusivity (geographic and first-time founders). This implies eligibility and outreach expectations rather than technical scoring rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of funded technology areas — broad, cross-sector coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: We fund startups across nearly all technology areas and markets like artificial intelligence, energy, medical devices, robotics, semiconductors, and many more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from a wide range of domains are eligible; the page lists representative areas and numerous success-story sectors to show breadth rather than a narrow topical focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company control and intellectual property expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer funding for early stage R&D and take no equity in your company — you retain full control over your team, the direction of your work, and your intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF grants are non-dilutive and allow awardees to maintain direction and ownership of IP. This is an important administrative/contractual expectation applicants can rely on when planning commercialization strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization emphasis / expectation of market impact
rubrics_metrics.description: We fund startups to build deep technologies for commercial success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program highlights commercialization as a key outcome (numerous success stories, mentions of first customers, scaling, acquisitions). Applicants should frame work in terms of potential pathways to market and commercial viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant resources and outreach (informational webinars/events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend our regular webinars to learn more. View events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF provides outreach and informational resources (webinars/events) to help applicants understand program expectations and the application process; prospective applicants are encouraged to use these resources.
